subject: battery

label: battery.mdl, in the place of the game's models/w_battery.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/scigun.mdl, models/w_gaussammo.mdl, models/w_squeak.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, D where the asset was A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline matches the brief's words: a chunky, tall prism (front and side views) with a chamfered base, a stubby striped tab on top and a grey cap. The tab leans at an angle in the front and back views, which reads as a lever rather than a plain stub, but it does not stick out or go missing in any view.

M2.reason: Measured 10.3 x 10.3 x 18.4 against the brief's 10 across and 18 high: 3% and 2% over, well within 15%.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked down to the small ones: grey metal body (present, chunky); glowing green panels (four large green panels, one per main face, with white side slabs between, in front-left and back-left views); hazard stripes (a yellow-and-black band around the lower body in every side view); a stubby handle on top (the striped tab on the top rim in front, left and back views). Nothing asked is missing. The red lamps and white slabs are extras, not losses.

M4.reason: Grey painted metal body, green glowing panels with a pale centre, yellow hazard stripes on dark metal. These are the colours and materials the brief names, and each region reads as its own material.

M5.reason: The markings are all there in their places (stripes, panel frames, lamps), but the green glow is a blotchy mosaic noise and the hazard stripes have smeared, uneven edges in the side and angle views. That is softer and dirtier than a crisp panel line and stripe at this scale. Not a must-have item.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, as the rubric asks for this asset. In the line-up of four it sits beside Valve's props and reads as one of them. The line-up test (asked three times, each in another order) picked the asset once in three, not twice or more.

M7.reason: Upright in the front view, with the central green panel and the top tab at the front, and it stands on its base in the side views. The brief says 'lying on the floor'; the asset rests on its base on the floor, which reads as the brief's meaning.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. Triangles: 116 against a bound of 116 (the larger of twice the median of 56, which is 112, and the third quartile, which is 116), so it passes at the limit. The below view shows the underside open with the background visible through it. A player cannot see that side of a prop lying on the floor, so it is Valve's practice and not a fault. The top and sides show nothing open, inside out or floating.
